what_to_detect: An attackers record in which a battle whose protector is a defending player of the attacking player (a Siege its controller attacks) is listed among the anchored attacker's legal defenders.
near_miss: A battle on the battlefield whose protector is the attacking player is absent from the attacker's legal defenders.
record_fields: snapshot battle entities (types, controller) for the battles not listed

what_to_detect: A combat damage step in which combat damage is dealt to a battle and a counter_change removes that many defense counters from it.
near_miss: A combat damage step in which a creature attacking a battle is blocked and deals its damage to the blocker, so the battle loses no defense counters.
record_fields: combat payload events: damage_dealt (cause, amount, subjects) and counter_change (counter_type DEFENSE, delta)

what_to_detect: A damage-dealing resolution whose effect half holds damage_dealt to a battle and a counter_change removing that many defense counters from it.
near_miss: A damage-dealing resolution whose damage goes to a creature or player, so no defense counter_change appears.
record_fields: effect half events: damage_dealt (amount, subjects), counter_change (counter_type, delta)

what_to_detect: A Siege at 0 defense counters that is the source of no triggered ability still on the stack is put into its owner's graveyard in the state-based check after a resolution.
near_miss: A Siege whose defense counters reach 0 while its own defeat trigger has triggered and not left the stack stays on the battlefield through the state-based check.
record_fields: snapshot stack objects and their sources
effect half counter_change and zone_change attributed unresolved (gen-3: every death of the state-based loop)
trigger record for the Siege's CounterRemovedOnce trigger, fired

what_to_detect: A blockers record whose anchored attacker is attacking a battle, in which creatures the battle's protector controls are listed as legal blockers.
near_miss: A creature controlled by a player other than the battle's protector is not a legal blocker of that attacker (in a two-player game such a creature is the attacking player's own and is never a candidate, so this side is rarely recorded).
record_fields: snapshot combat.attacking of the anchored attacker, battle entity controller

what_to_detect: An attackers record in which a battle whose control passed to the attacking player (so its former protector, now its controller, was replaced by an opponent) is listed among the attacker's legal defenders.
near_miss: A battle the attacking player still protects is absent from the attacker's legal defenders.
record_fields: earlier control_change event on the battle
